note: Piggul is a technical term for sacrificial flesh that has become ritually spoiled by being kept too long (cf. 19:7); it is distinct from to'evah, which the KJV also renders "abomination."
Shoq denotes the leg/thigh (the upper hind leg), not the shoulder; the KJV term recurs in 7:33-34, 8:25-26, 9:21, 10:14-15.

kjv: the anointing of Aaron, and of the anointing of his sons
mine: the portion of Aaron and the portion of his sons
note: Mishchah here is the homonym meaning "allotted portion" (cf. Num 18:8), referring to the priestly share of the offerings, not the rite of anointing.
